Lena / Jared —

Thanks, received. Looping Aditya to provide the technical details and sample export. Quick answers up front to your field checklist:
- Fields: timestamp, request_id, client_id (API key id), endpoint, response_status, latency_ms are captured for all API requests. We store headers metadata (but not request/response bodies unless explicitly enabled and consented) — bodies are not logged by default for privacy.
- user_id: included when the caller supplies an application user id in the x-redwood-user header; otherwise null.
- Sequence detection: exports include an incremental event_id per log row and we can also sign exports with a hash for tamper-evidence. For Dedicated/Private customers we offer WORM retention policies.

Attaching a redacted sample export (CSV) and a short tech note that describes retention and immutability options.

Next steps:

Thanks — Marissa

Hi Lena / Jared —

Adding a few technical clarifications from the infra side:

1) Admin activity logs: capture user identity, action (create/update/delete), resource (user, role, model deployment, routing policy), IP, timestamp, and request_id. These are available via the Console audit endpoint and can be exported as CSV/JSON.

2) API request logs: as Marissa noted — timestamp, request_id, client_id, endpoint, response_status, latency_ms. We redact request/response bodies by default. For customers that need payload-level logs for debugging, we can enable body logging in Private deployments under contractual terms; bodies are encrypted at rest and access is audited.

3) Exportability & integrity: Exports support CSV and newline-delimited JSON; each exported batch includes an incremental event_id and an SHA256 manifest file for integrity verification. For Dedicated/Private, we can enable append-only WORM buckets and provide signed manifests.

4) Retention: default retention for hosted customers is 90 days for API logs and 365 days for admin logs; Dedicated/Private are configurable per contract up to multi-year.

5) Delivery options: direct S3 export, syslog/forwarding to your SIEM, or API listing for programmatic ingestion.

I've attached a one-pager and the sample CSV with column headers for your security team to review. Happy to review these during Wed 10am PT — sending a calendar invite now.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
